name: Pluto
fact: The largest known Kuiper Belt body and the first object beyond Neptune ever discovered (1930). Reclassified from planet to dwarf planet by the IAU in 2006.
bio: Pluto's 248-year orbit is highly eccentric (e = 0.249) and inclined 17° to the ecliptic — so its orbit dips inside Neptune's for 20 years per cycle and rises well above the planetary plane. Surface temperatures swing wide enough that the thin nitrogen atmosphere thickens near perihelion and freezes back onto the surface near aphelion. The mutual tidal lock with Charon makes the pair a true binary system.
